negative_reviews.author: Lee Z
negative_reviews.text:
Food was delicious and the restaurant was beautiful.

Only complaint with the food is the menu is very limited, they don't have sushi nigiri listed but you can get in the combo piece things.

Service:

What really upset me is while I was eating, a lady asked my dad if she can clean the table. While I'm eating my last piece of sushi she takes the plate I'm using to eat from under my chin. This makes customers feel horribly rushed and also increases the risk I drop sushi on the table or on my pants

Next they bring out my parents foods and mine does not come out for another 10 minutes after so by the time they are almost done, I am just starting.

I got an iced tea also, they explained they don't serve it but they can make me it. They then proceed to serve me iced tea which was crystal clear because it wasn't steeped at all .

If you can't make the item even remotely resemble ice tea, then do not serve it or give me a cup of ice with the hot tea.

negative_reviews.author: B C
negative_reviews.text: The price is reasonable, but the tonkotsu ramen is not so authentic.

negative_reviews.author: Leila A
negative_reviews.text: Unfortunately the food was a major disappointment. For such a selective menu, it is expected that the dishes available have been somewhat perfected, but the sushi did not taste fresh, the chicken karaage had an overwhelming mouthful of flour. The snow crab had some shell left. It’s a shame as the service is incredibly lovely, but the food was incredibly mediocre. If you want atmosphere and do not care too much for the quality of the food, the interior is cool and the servers are lovely. But for food , go elsewhere.

negative_reviews.author: T S
negative_reviews.text:
For reference Ive just finished my meal maybe about an hour or so ago, so keep this review in mind. I’m a sushi lover who’s visited the likes of Dinings SW3, Roka, Zuma, Sticks and Sushi, Sushi Samba and more. I’ve also visited Ukiyo in Covent Garden 5 times - the only other handroll bar prior to the opening of Maki Nori, so naturally wanted to try somewhere in hopes of change, but this restaurant doesn’t qualify at all.

Upon arrival, I can say that the place is very aesthetically pleasing and immediately peaked my interest. I was extremely excited to try the food as I’d seen various promotional tiktoks floating around prior. And again, the place was well designed with a generous chefs counter which allows you to feel a part of the experience. The waiters are attentive and welcoming. However, unfortunately the experience fell gravely short of basic standards leaving me and my partner without the will to ever return.

Firstly, we were sat at the counter, however despite it being relatively empty, the counter itself was uncleaned with various rice grains lingering and obvious residue which felt unhygienic. This was also  echoed by no given hand wipes for sanitation which is expected of a hand roll style establishment . Napkins were cheap and basic. We would have appreciated some material cloths. And the blue plates provided were randomly placed with no explanation for use. I would’ve liked to see more chefs at the counter as the limited chefs caused missed items for other customers and a mistaken item for my meal.

The food is where the real disappointment hit hard. Personally I would give it a 4-5/10 at most. The fish was not fresh at all. It had a stale/off taste generally and with other cuts not tasting of anything at all. Some pieces were dried on the surface and lacked rich colour indicating that it had been there for a while. The temperature of the fish was clearly not managed well and was not cool which further amplified this stale nature. The rice - the grain was far too large and extremely dry. This was a really poor choice when I compare to other restaurants of the same category. It was distasteful and unpleasant especially in the Nigiri and chefs omakase. Another customer queried this same concern while we were sat, which solidified my rating. The taste was lacklustre missing the rice vinegar, fluff, and overall fragrance. Should scrap that brand entirely.

Everything looked visually good but, the taste was incredibly disappointing. To be honest, this is the main factor I observe when comparing each  restaurant to their counterparts. Everything must be seamless, well curated, swiftly conducted and undeniably fresh. At one point I didn’t even want to finish the chefs selection, but out of respect to the chef who had plated it, I did.

If anything I just want to reiterate the importance of freshness in Japanese cuisine and food safety. I think it’s paramount that there are less pre-made items to encompass the omakase dining experience. My overall recommendation is to not visit this place until adequate change has been applied.

negative_reviews.author: Jack Leung
negative_reviews.text: Rice is undercooked, service, what service have I had ? There’s barely any space in our area, I don’t recommend this place
